abstract: We investigate quantum computational complexity of calculating partition functions of Ising models. We construct a quantum algorithm for an additive approximation of Ising partition functions on square lattices. To this end, we utilize the overlap mapping developed by Van den Nest, Dür, and Briegel [Phys. Rev. Lett. 98, 117207 (2007)] and its interpretation through measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC). We specify an algorithmic domain, on which the proposed algorithm works, and an approximation scale, which determines the accuracy of the approximation. We show that the proposed algorithm does a nontrivial task, which would be intractable on any classical computer, by showing the problem solvable by the proposed quantum algorithm are BQP-complete. In the construction of the BQP-complete problem coupling strengths and magnetic fields take complex values. However, the Ising models that are of central interest in statistical physics and computer science consist of real coupling strengths and magnetic fields. Thus we extend the algorithmic domain of the proposed algorithm to such a real physical parameter region and calculate the approximation scale explicitly. We found that the overlap mapping and its MBQC interpretation improves the approximation scale exponentially compared to a straightforward constant depth quantum algorithm. On the other hand, the proposed quantum algorithm also provides us a partial evidence that there exist no efficient classical algorithm for a multiplicative approximation of the Ising partition functions even on the square lattice. This result supports that the proposed quantum algorithm does a nontrivial task also in the physical parameter region.

specification.problem: Construct a quantum algorithm for additive approximation of Ising partition functions on square lattices using the overlap mapping of Van den Nest, Dür and Briegel and its MBQC interpretation. Specify the algorithmic domain and approximation scale, show BQP-completeness with complex couplings and fields, and extend to real parameters with an explicit approximation scale.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the problem statement and a few standard background equations for the Ising partition function and additive approximation. The detailed overlap mapping, MBQC circuit, and approximation-scale formula are not given in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: a square-lattice graph-state-like MBQC resource state, with exact form not specified in the abstract.

steps.description: Map the Ising instance (J_ij, h_i) to an overlap between a lattice stabilizer-type state and a product state, following the overlap mapping, so that Z is proportional to the overlap (details assumed).
Interpret the overlap as an MBQC computation: prepare the lattice resource state and apply single-qubit measurements with angles set by the couplings and fields (details assumed).
Estimate the overlap amplitude by repeated runs to precision epsilon, giving an additive estimate of Z at scale Delta.

specification.measurement: Assumed: single-qubit measurements of the lattice qubits in bases set by the couplings and fields (MBQC), then a final readout of the output qubit; its statistics over repeated runs estimate the real and imaginary parts of the overlap proportional to Z. Exact angles are not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: average the measurement outcomes over repeated runs, with number of runs scaling as 1/epsilon^2, to estimate the overlap; rescale by the known normalization to obtain an estimate of Z with additive error epsilon times Delta. The normalization and Delta are not given in the abstract.
